newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity eases on lower cash, weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity eases on lower cash, weather.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading lower Thursday under some weakness from cheaper physical power prices and forecasts for some cooler weather in the West, industry sources said.
Generation units in the West were also returning to service, lending some weakness to power futures, the traders noted.
The 540 megawatt (MW) San Juan unit 4 coal-fired plant in New Mexico was said to be back at full power Wednesday night after being shut last weekend to repair a boiler tube leak.

The 360 MW unit 1 at the Springerville coal-fired power plant in Arizona was back to full power early Thursday after operating near half capacity for the past several days, sources familiar with the plant's operations said Thursday.
Also, units 1 and 3, each at 750 MW, at the Navajo coal-fired power plant near Page, Arizona, were back to full power, sources familiar with the plant's operations said.

As of 1230 EDT, May Palo Verde was trading down 23 cents at $17.90 per megawatt hour (MWh) after exchanges at $17.80-18.20, while June was down 15 cents at $18.20 after reaching as high as $18.40 per MWh.
September PV had traded down six cents at $23.00 per MWh.
May California Oregon Border (COB) was trading down 15 cents at $13.40 after reaching as high as $13.65, while June was steady at $12.35 from exchanges at $12.15-12.50 per MWh.
August COB had traded down 30 cents at $18.30 per MWh.
NYMEX said an estimated 277 COB and 104 PV contracts had traded as of 1200 EDT.
As of 1235 EDT, May Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading up one cent at $2.07 per million British thermal units.
Late Wednesday, the 550 MW unit 4 at the Jim Bridger generating complex in Wyoming returned to service, while the plant's 550 MW unit 1 was in the process of restart.
The 408 MW unit 3 at the Craig power plant in Colorado was also set to startup today following a spring maintenance outage.

Temperatures in the Pacific Northwest were forecast to be three to six degrees below normal in the mountains and near normal elsewhere for Friday. Early next week, the Pacific Northwest was expected to see temperatures three to 10 degrees above normal.
In the Southwest, rain and thunderstorms were likely to continue in the north and east, with milder and dryer conditions called for by Tuesday and Wednesday.
COB open interest for April 23 fell 37 to 4,470, while PV open interest rose 233 to 5,486, NYMEX said.
